maria (eng-runtime): Heads-up — we just flipped the hybrid prefetch + coalesce runtime policy to default on all hosted clusters :tada:

kavya (bench): numbers look solid. p50 down ~18%, p95 down ~22%, token cost down ~17% on our standard gen workload (100M req sample). Saved a bunch on small-seq tail cases.

sam (eng): For folks curious about the change: we now do adaptive lookahead prefetching + sequence-aware coalescing. It avoids polling short-lived requests into tiny microbatches and merges compatible KV prefixes.

maria (eng-runtime): Quick command we used for the canary run:
```
./bench/run.sh --profile=std-gen --policy=prefetch-coalesce-v2 --samples=1000000
```
output snippet: 
```
latency.p50: 121.5ms -> 99.4ms
latency.p95: 489.2ms -> 381.6ms
cost.token.unit: 0.0184 -> 0.0153
```

alec (prodops): Deployed across regions with rolling 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% steps, auto-fallback to prefetch-v1 if latency regression detected. No sig incidents, fallback not triggered. deploy-bot: rolled v=2026.3.12-3 into prod clusters eu/west1,us-central.

mel (pm): Huge win for the optimization roadmap. Can we add a short blurb for the weekly product update? A one-liner about cost reductions and reliability improvements would be great.

kavya (bench): I'll drop a perf dashboard link and the perf-run notebook in #eng-runtime later today. Initial graphs: heatmap of seq-lens vs batch-size shows much higher coalescing on 8-64 token requests.

sam (eng): Notes for on-call: watch for elevated KV miss rates for models with heavy prefix variance — we tuned eviction thresholds but it's the main risk. If p95 climbs >+10% for 5m, rollback command is: `./deploy/rollback.sh prefetch-coalesce-v2`

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks everyone — big shout-out to bench + infra for moving quickly. If anyone sees unexpected user-facing regressions tag me or @alec. :rocket:
